### R5-01 · Quick review

SCAN vs SEARCH in EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

SCAN reads every row of the table (or index) in order. SEARCH uses an index (or the primary key) to jump straight to matching rows.
</details>

<sub>Source: [lecture5 L328-332](../sources/lecture5.txt) *“The plan is to scan movies”*</sub>

### R5-02 · Predict the output

Dataset `movies`:

```sql
EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN SELECT "title" FROM "movies" WHERE "id" = 114709;
```
What is printed?

A. `SCAN movies`
B. `SEARCH movies USING INTEGER PRIMARY KEY (rowid=?)`
C. `SEARCH movies USING INDEX title_index (title=?)`

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**B**. Primary keys are indexed automatically, so no CREATE INDEX is needed.
</details>

<sub>Source: [lecture5 L427-430](../sources/lecture5.txt) *“using integer primary key”*</sub>

### R5-03 · Concept check

What makes an index *covering* for a query?

A. It has more than one column
B. It contains every column the query needs from that table, so no table lookup
C. It is on the primary key
D. It has a WHERE clause

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**B**. Multi-column is common but not sufficient. What matters is that the query never has to go back to the table.
</details>

<sub>Source: [lecture5 L483-488](../sources/lecture5.txt) *“It's one in which the query data can be found only by searching the index.”*</sub>

### R5-04 · Concept check

Two costs of an index (lecture's B-tree discussion)?

A. More disk space and slower INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE
B. Slower SELECTs and less space
C. It locks the table forever
D. It disables foreign keys

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**A**. An index is a sorted copy plus pointers, which costs space, and every write must also update the tree.
</details>

<sub>Source: [lecture5 L852-857](../sources/lecture5.txt) *“if I want to insert something into this structure, it'll take me more time”*</sub>

### R5-05 · Predict the output

Dataset `movies` after setup:

```sql
CREATE INDEX "recents" ON "movies" ("title") WHERE "year" = 2023;
```
```sql
EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN SELECT "title" FROM "movies" WHERE "year" = 1998;
```
What is printed?

A. `SCAN movies`
B. `SCAN movies USING COVERING INDEX recents`
C. `SEARCH movies USING INDEX recents`

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**A**. 1998 rows aren't in the partial index, so it can't be used.
</details>

<sub>Source: [lecture5 L917-924](../sources/lecture5.txt) *“Now I'm only back to scanning movies.”*</sub>

### R5-06 · Concept check

You DROP three large indexes. What happens to the database file size?

A. Shrinks immediately
B. Unchanged until VACUUM
C. Grows
D. The file is deleted

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**B**. Freed pages are only marked reusable. VACUUM returns them to the OS.
</details>

<sub>Source: [lecture5 L996-999](../sources/lecture5.txt) *“we don't actually shrink our database file”*</sub>

### R5-07 · Quick review

Spell out ACID in one line each.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

Atomicity, all or nothing. Consistency, never violate constraints. Isolation, concurrent transactions don't interfere. Durability, committed data survives crashes.
</details>

<sub>Source: [lecture5 L1110-1127](../sources/lecture5.txt) *“A stands for atomicity”*</sub>

### R5-08 · Predict the output

Dataset `bank`:

```sql
BEGIN TRANSACTION;
UPDATE "accounts" SET "balance" = "balance" + 10 WHERE "id" = 2;
ROLLBACK;
SELECT "balance" FROM "accounts" WHERE "id" = 2;
```
What is printed?

A. `20`
B. `30`
C. `ERROR: cannot rollback`

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**A**. ROLLBACK undoes everything since BEGIN.
</details>

<sub>Source: [lecture5 L1263-1267](../sources/lecture5.txt) *“think about it as if this transaction never even”*</sub>

### R5-09 · Concept check

Which SQLite lock lets many connections read at once?

A. EXCLUSIVE
B. SHARED
C. UNLOCKED

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**B**. SHARED is for readers. A writer needs EXCLUSIVE, which blocks everyone else.
</details>

<sub>Source: [lecture5 L1476-1479](../sources/lecture5.txt) *“A shared lock means I'm only reading.”*</sub>
